published_figures.source: Boeing D6-58326-1 rev F, 2024; FAA TCDS A20WE
published_figures.figure: Figure 3.3.1, page 3-13: FAR take-off runway length, standard day, sea level, flaps 20, air conditioning off, at 875,000 lb - about 10,500 ft, read from the chart.

FAR 25.121(b), the 747-400's certification basis (A20WE): with one engine out, the take-off flaps, the gear up and V2, a four-engined aircraft climbs at no less than 3.0%. No figure above that is published; 10% bounds a model gone wrong.
Level at 35,000 ft at full throttle, it must reach its cruise Mach, 0.85 (the payload-range chart's, figure 3.2.1), and its drag rise hold it within 0.03 of its Mmo, 0.92 (A20WE).
A20WE: maximum operating altitude 45,100 ft. As light as it flies, at full throttle, it still climbs there at 300 ft/min, the margin that makes an altitude a thrust-limited ceiling.
published_figures.plan_speeds: The slowest, 220 kt, is 5 kt over the slowest that held: it publishes no stall speed, so has no approach speed, and the sweep began at 160 kt (`plan-speeds 747-400 160`); below 215 kt it came down 500 ft before it reached its circle (at 210 kt, its 6,381 m circle); 215 kt held all four ways. The fastest, 300 kt, a fifth over its start speed, held all four ways. Measured again on 2026-11-01 (linux-release, `plan-speeds 747-400`), once she had an approach speed - Boeing's 153 kt at 630,000 lb, 167.4 kt at this weight - and her flapped lift and elevator came from NASA CR-2144: swept up from 168 kt, below 208 kt she came down 500 ft before she reached her circle; 208 kt held all four ways, so the slowest is 213 (it was 220). The fastest is unchanged.
published_figures.glide_speeds: 230 kt; from 213, the slowest a route may fly it, to 225 it stalled. Measured again on 2026-11-01 (linux-release), once her elevator's power came from NASA CR-2144 (tools/make_747_400.py): it was 235, 230 having stalled.
published_figures.takeoff_speeds: Rotation: from 100 kt in 5 kt steps, the first that lifted her off within 15 kt of itself, unwrecked, inside the 3,500 m runway, and never 5 kt slower once off, was 155 kt; 160 is written, 5 kt to spare. Rotated at 100 to 150 kt she ran on, and left the ground more than 15 kt past it - at 168 kt from 115 to 150. The climb away: asked 170 to 260 kt, at 500 ft she was never slower than 163.8 kt, 6 kt under the slowest asked - the slowest she climbs away at with her nose held no higher than the take-off autopilot holds it - which is written rounded up. At flaps 20, the take-off field length's, held to 500 ft, and 754,313 lb, the weight her model flies a plan at. Measured again on 2026-10-09 (linux-release): until then the take-off raised its flaps at once from 200 ft, so the climb away was read with them running up, at 187.1 kt. And again on 2026-10-13 (linux-release), once her rotation was held to her three degrees a second on her wheels: the rotation is unchanged, and she leaves a little lower and slower, so the slowest climb away fell from 165.2 kt to 163.8, which rounds up to 165; the measurement now writes no climb away within ten knots of her rotation speed (sim/takeoff_trial.cpp, 14 CFR 25.107(c)(2)), so it stays 170. And again on 2026-11-01 (linux-release), once her main gear stood at Boeing's station 1404 and her flapped lift came from NASA CR-2144 and CR-1756 (tools/make_747_400.py): rotated from 100 to 140 kt she ran on and left the ground at 156 to 157 kt; from 145 she lifted off within 15 kt, so the rotation, with 5 kt to spare, is 150 (it was 160); she unsticks at 158 kt, 1,694 m along, and the slowest she climbed away at was 169.3 kt, written as 170.
published_figures.approach: Boeing, Aerodrome Reference Code and Approach Speeds, rev A, August 2026: 153 kt at the 630,000 lb maximum landing weight; flaps 30.
published_figures.landing_distance: Figure 3.4.2, page 3-36: F.A.R. landing runway length, flaps 30, dry runway, sea level, zero wind, at the 574,000 lb maximum landing weight above - about 6,200 ft, read from the chart. Factor 1: a landing field length is already the demonstrated distance over 0.6, the margin of 14 CFR 121.195(b), so it is the runway needed as it stands.
published_figures.no_cg_limits: Her weight and centre-of-gravity envelope is not published: her type certificate data sheets refer to her flight manual (FAA A20WE, revision 58: her C.G. range in "the appropriate FAA Approved Airplane Flight Manual", D6-13703) and her weight and balance manual (EASA IM.A.196), neither of them public. The one public figure found (2026-10-24), 15.5 to 33.0% of her chord for a 747-400BCF's take-off at one weight (NTSB AAR-15/01), is one weight's, not her envelope.
